First release candidate for testing open[flow], with an emphasis on mix[flow] on Apple silicon. This is a prerelease for evaluation; keep a backup of your library and use a copy for testing.

## Downloads

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `mix-flow-0.1.0-rc.1-arm64.dmg` | mix[flow]: local stem separation, track preparation and four-deck playback. This is the installer for the mix test. |
| `set-flow-0.1.0-rc.1-arm64.dmg` | set[flow], the Ableton Live session manager. |
| `visual-flow-0.1.0-rc.1-arm64.dmg` | visual[flow], the visual performance app. |
| `SessionBridge-0.1.0-rc.1.zip` | Max for Live bridge device for set[flow] and visual[flow]. Keep its three files together. |

The apps target Apple silicon. The release workflow signs and notarizes both apps and disk images, then requires Gatekeeper and stapled-ticket verification before attaching them. mix[flow] runs independently of Live and the bridge.

## mix[flow] first test

1. Install from the DMG and launch from Finder.
2. Choose a fresh library folder and import local audio. Imports copy files into the library.
3. Generate stems. The first separation downloads a managed Python environment, locked dependencies and model weights; an internet connection and additional disk space are needed. No separate Python or FFmpeg installation is required.
4. Check setup progress, cancellation and retry, then complete a separation.
5. Prepare and load tracks, try multiple decks and stem playback, quit and reopen to check persistence.

Headphone monitoring uses outputs 3/4 on an interface that exposes at least four channels; master uses 1/2. It is not a separate headphone-device selector. Hardware routing and clean-machine first-run behavior still need testing on the receiving Mac. Automatic updates remain disabled; install a later version explicitly.

## Release preparation

- Keep the complete three-minute tempo regression fixture, with an isolated 15-second CI timeout.
- Compile Electron bundles in Linux CI without invoking macOS-native preparation; actual packaging still builds the native tools.
- Backport electron-builder's upstream temporary-keychain password correction. Certificate import and keychain authentication retain their distinct passwords; signing and notarization checks remain mandatory.
- Include the completed Electron 44.2.0, happy-dom and qs updates on main.

The preceding nightly passed signing, notarization, Gatekeeper verification and publication. This RC has its own release checks; that does not replace testing import, downloads, separation, playback and persistence on a clean Mac. Changes to `bridge/src/lom.ts` require Live/device testing and are not covered by the automated suite.

For installation details, see [Installing](https://github.com/ryangavin/better-session-view/wiki/Installing). Report the version, macOS version, audio hardware and steps when reporting a problem.
